key_insight: Magnesium alloy joints are difficult to weld reliably, so the review argues that solid-state and optimized hybrid joining methods are increasingly important for defect control and joint integrity.
engineering_relevance: For lightweight automotive and advanced structural design, selecting the right welding process for Mg alloys directly affects crack risk, microstructure, and mechanical performance.
method: Reviewed scientific databases and patents using relevant welding keywords
Compared fusion, friction, diffusion, explosive, and hybrid welding methods for Mg alloys
Highlighted GTAW, GMAW, LBW, and FSW as key processes for AZ-series alloys
evidence_signal: The paper is a literature-and-patent review that synthesizes reported process outcomes, weld microstructure effects, and property trends rather than presenting new experiments.
watch_item: Mg alloys remain highly crack-sensitive, so process variables, dissimilar-joint compatibility, and defect control must be carefully managed before industrial deployment.
paper_title: Welding Techniques for Magnesium Alloy Joints: A Comprehensive Review
